biological.citation: Kim et al. 2013 - CHD7 interacts with BMP R-SMADs to epigenetically regulate cardiogenesis in mice (PMID: 24293546)
biological.summary: Yeast two-hybrid and biochemical assays identified CHD7 as an interaction partner of the BMP pathway mediators SMAD1/5/8 in embryonic heart. CHD7 associates in a BMP-dependent manner with Nkx2.5 enhancers and is required for their active epigenetic signature and for Nkx2.5 expression. Chd7 inactivation in mice impairs BMP-regulated cardiogenic processes.

biological.citation: Chd7 cooperates with Sox10 and regulates the onset of CNS myelination and remyelination (PMID: 26928066)
biological.summary: Chd7 is a direct transcriptional target of Olig2 and Smarca4/Brg1 and is required for proper onset of CNS myelination and remyelination. Genome-occupancy analyses showed it interacts with Sox10 and targets enhancers of myelinogenic genes, including Osterix (Sp7) and Creb3l2.

biological.citation: CHD7 regulates bone-fat balance by suppressing PPAR-γ signaling (PMID: 35418650)
biological.summary: Conditional Chd7 knockout in bone marrow MSCs and preosteoblasts causes low bone mass and high marrow adiposity. Loss of Chd7 relieves restriction of PPAR-γ, which then associates with H3K4me3 and activates adipogenic genes, shifting the balance from osteogenesis to adipogenesis.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Perturb-tracing enables scalable high-content discovery of 3D genome regulators
biological.summary: In a pooled CRISPR loss-of-function imaging screen in human cells, CHD7, previously known to promote local chromatin openness, was found to compact chromatin over long range in a CTCF-dependent manner. It also facilitates a multi-TAD compaction effect of cohesin.

biological.citation: Hiraoka et al. 2016 - CHD7, Oct3/4, Sox2, and Nanog control FoxD3 expression during mouse neural crest-derived stem cell formation (PMID: 27579714)
biological.summary: CHD7, Oct3/4, Sox2 and Nanog occupy conserved FoxD3 regulatory regions (mE1–mE3) in a BMP2/Wnt3a-dependent manner. siRNA knockdown of CHD7 suppressed FoxD3 expression, which in turn promotes Sox10 expression, placing CHD7 downstream of BMP2/Wnt3a signaling in neural crest-derived stem cell formation. H3K4 methylation is also required.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Chd7 and Sox2 cooperate to regulate development of the inner ear
biological.summary: Chd7 and Sox2 are dynamically co-expressed in the developing mouse ear, and CHD7 acts genetically upstream of Sox2. Chd7Gt/+;Sox2CreER/+ double heterozygotes show early postnatal death, malformed inner ear and increased cell death, with a critical window at E9.5. Lhx1 was the most upregulated gene, and Chd7;Lhx1 double heterozygotes had worse cochlear hypoplasia.

biological.citation: CHD7 in oocytes is essential for female fertility (PMID: 35402599)
biological.summary: CHD7 is highly expressed across all stages of oocyte development. Oocyte-specific deletion (Gdf9-Cre;Chd7f/f) causes infertility or sub-fertility, decreased follicle numbers at all stages and increased granulosa cell apoptosis.

biological.citation: let-7 miRNAs inhibit CHD7 expression and control auditory-sensory progenitor cell behavior in the developing inner ear (PMID: 32816902)
biological.summary: An evolutionarily conserved let-7-5p binding site was found in chicken, human and mouse Chd7. let-7g overexpression in mice limits CHD7 expression in developing inner ear, retina and brain, implicating CHD7 as a mediator of let-7 effects on hair cell differentiation.

biological.citation: The Genomic and Epigenomic Landscape of Double-Negative Metastatic Prostate Cancer (PMID: 37289025)
biological.summary: CHD7 is amplified in AR-/NE- mCRPC. Methylation changes in CHD7 candidate enhancers were linked to elevated CHD7 expression in AR-/NE+ tumors.

biological.citation: Atlas of imprinted and allele-specific DNA methylation in the human body (PMID: 40069157)
biological.summary: Tissue-specific, maternal allele-specific DNA methylation of CHD7 was validated across human cell types. This offers a potential mechanism for the paternal bias in inheritance of CHARGE syndrome.
